Analytical grade reagents from Sigma Aldrich (USA) were used without further modification. Some of the reagents are: orthophosphoric acid (H3PO4), (CAS No: 7664 – 38 - 2), HCl (Hydrochloric acid) (CAS: 7697 – 37 - 2), sodium hydroxide (NaOH) (Carlo Erba CAS: 1310–73–2), magnetic stirrer (Bante MS300), titanium isopropoxide, pH meter (Milwaukee instrument: MW102 PRO 2-in-1 pH and Temperature meter), oven (GENLAB N30C), and furnace (Searchtech SX-5–12). The raw coconut shells were collected from Omu-Aran local market, Longitude (5.1026 ° E) and Latitude (8.1386 ° N), Kwara State, Nigeria.

The molecular functional components of CSAC-P-TiO2—NC were determined using Attenuated Total Reflection-Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy (Bruker Optics, Germany), equipped with a single-reflection Ge crystal attenuated total reflectance (ATR, Pike technologies), with measurements conducted in the range of 4000–400 cm-1d.Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA)

The thermal stability of the prepared CSAC-P-TiO2—NC was performed by carrying out Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA, Q500, USA) under an air atmosphere from room temperature to 1000 °C with a heating rate of 10 °C/min.e.Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM)

The elemental composition and binding energy of the nanocomposite were determined using the X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) equipment with high-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (HRXPS ESCALAB Xi+ Thermo-Fisher Scientific, USA)g.Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) Equipped with Energy Dispersive X-ray (EDX)

The surface morphology of prepared CSAC-P-TiO2—NC was visualized by SEM analysis using a field-emission scanning electron microscope (FESEM, Thermo Fisher Verios 460 L, USA) equipped with an Oxford Instrument energy dispersive-X-ray.

The thermal stability and behaviour of CSAC-P-TiO2—NC was ascertained by performing Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and derivative thermogravimetry (DTG) presented in Fig. 3. From the plot, loss in weight and transition in phase occurred at two different levels; the first occurred from 30 °C to 400 °C accounting for a weight loss of 0.033 mg representing 1.028% percentage loss in weight. The last weight loss occurred from 400 °C to 973.51 °C resulting in 2.922% percent loss in weight and 0.094 mg weight loss. The total weight loss at the end of the analysis was 3.95% percent 3.94 mg loss in weight of CSAC-P-TiO2—NC. At higher temperature above 500 °C, an increase in weight loss was observed which may be attributed to the evaporation of moisture trapped within interstitial axis of the nanocomposite [9]. The overall weight loss was <5.0% and lower than that obtained for the nanocomposite of zinc oxide reported by [22].

steps.title: Prepare carbonized coconut shell powder
steps.instruction: Sort, wash and dry raw coconut shells to remove dirt; carbonize 1 kg of the dried shells at 400 °C for 1 h; grind the carbonized material with a mortar and pestle and sieve through a 0.15 mm mesh; label the resulting fine powder as CS.

steps.title: Chemically activate carbon with phosphoric acid
steps.instruction: In a beaker add 1000 mL of 0.5 M H₃PO₄, then add 1000 g of CS and heat while stirring until a paste forms; transfer the paste to a furnace set at 400 °C and heat for 1 h; cool, rinse thoroughly with distilled water until the suspension reaches pH 7.0; dry the activated carbon in an oven at 100 °C for 2 h; store the dried material in an airtight container and label it CSAC‑P.

steps.title: Synthesize TiO₂ nanoparticles (hydrothermal)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mL titanium tetraisopropoxide in 30 mL ethanol while stirring continuously for 30 min on a magnetic stirrer; add a few drops of distilled water to obtain a white dispersion; filter the resulting precipitate with filter paper and wash the solid 4–5 times with distilled water; dry the washed solid in an oven at 100 °C for 5 h; calcine the dried powder at 500 °C for 3 h; allow to cool, label the product TiO₂‑NPs and store.

steps.title: Prepare CSAC‑P‑TiO₂ nanocomposite
steps.instruction: Mix CSAC‑P and TiO₂‑NPs at a mass ratio of 5:1; dissolve 1.0 g CSAC‑P in 100 mL distilled water and ultrasonicate for 30 min; separately dissolve 1.0 g of the CSAC‑P/TiO₂‑NPs mixture in 20 mL distilled water and ultrasonicate for 30 min; combine the two suspensions and sonicate the mixture for an additional 30 min; filter the resulting suspension with filter paper; dry the filtered solid at 100 °C overnight in an oven; after cooling, label the dried material CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC and store appropriately.

steps.title: Determine pH of nanocomposite suspension
steps.instruction: Measure 100 mL distilled water into a beaker, add 1.0 g CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC and boil for 5 min on a hot plate; add a further 100 mL distilled water, allow the mixture to cool, then measure the pH with a calibrated pH meter.

steps.title: Measure bulk density
steps.instruction: Weigh an empty 10 mL measuring cylinder (w₁); fill the cylinder with CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC, tap gently to expel trapped air, and weigh again (w₂); compute bulk density using BulkDensity = (w₂ − w₁) / v × 100, where v is the cylinder volume (10 mL).

steps.title: Determine moisture content
steps.instruction: Weigh an empty crucible, add 1.0 g CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC and record the combined weight (w₁); oven‑dry the crucible with sample at 100 °C for 5 h; cool in a desiccator for 24 h and weigh again (w₂); calculate moisture % = (w₂ / w₁) × 100.

steps.title: Determine ash content
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat an empty crucible at 100 °C for 5 min, cool and weigh; add 1.0 g CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC, then place the crucible in a furnace at 500 °C for 1.5 h; cool in a desiccator for 24 h and weigh; compute ash % = (w₁ / w₂) × 100 where w₁ is the weight before heating and w₂ after heating.

steps.title: Surface area by Saer method
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 g CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC to a 250 mL conical flask containing 50 mL NaCl solution; adjust the pH from 4 to 9 using 0.1 M HCl and 0.1 M NaOH, recording the total volume V (mL) of acid or base added; calculate surface area S (m² g⁻¹) with S = 32 V − 25.

steps.title: Determine volatile matter
steps.instruction: Weigh an empty crucible, add 1.0 g CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC and record the weight (w₁); heat the crucible in a furnace at 500 °C for 10 min; cool and weigh the residue (w₂); calculate volatile % = (w₁ / w₂) × 100.

steps.title: Determine point of zero charge (pHₚzc)
steps.instruction: Weigh 1.0 g CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC into several 0.1 M NaCl solution flasks; adjust each flask’s initial pH to values ranging from 2 to 12 using 0.1 M HCl or 0.1 M NaOH; seal the flasks and shake for 24 h; measure the final pH of each flask; plot ΔpH (final − initial) versus initial pH; the pH at which ΔpH = 0 is the pHₚzc.

steps.title: Iodine number (porosity test)
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 mL of a standardized iodine stock solution; add 0.5 g CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC to the iodine solution and stir continuously; place the mixture on a shaker for 60 min; filter the suspension; take 20 mL of the filtrate and titrate against 0.1 M Na₂S₂O₃; calculate the iodine number using 1 mg g⁻¹ = (B − S B) × V × M_W / (2 × 53.81 × W) where B = volume of thiosulfate for blank, S B = volume for sample, V = 20 mL, M_W = iodine molar mass (251.83 g mol⁻¹), and W = mass of adsorbent (0.5 g).

steps.title: Boehm titration (acidic/basic groups)
steps.instruction: Weigh 1.0 g CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC into four separate beakers containing: (i) 0.1 M NaOH, (ii) 0.5 M Na₂CO₃, (iii) 0.1 M NaHCO₃, and (iv) 0.1 M HCl; place the beakers on an electric shaker for 48 h; back‑titrate the basic solutions with 0.1 M HCl and the acidic solutions with 0.1 M NaOH; calculate the number of oxygen‑containing functional groups using Fx = (V_bx − V_ex) × M × D / (M_t) where V_bx and V_ex are titrant volumes for blank and extract, M is titrant molarity, D is dilution factor, and M_t is mass of sample.

steps.title: BET and BJH surface area analysis
steps.instruction: Load an appropriate amount of CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC into the BET instrument (Quantachrome Autosorb IQ2, FL, USA); perform N₂ adsorption–desorption isotherms at liquid nitrogen temperature; calculate BET surface area, BJH pore volume, pore radius, and pore size using the instrument’s software.

steps.title: X‑ray diffraction (XRD) analysis
steps.instruction: Pack CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC into an XRD sample holder; scan 2θ from ~20° to 80° using Cu Kα radiation (λ = 0.1504 nm); identify diffraction peaks (e.g., 2θ = 25.3°, 37.7°, 47.9°, 53.8°, 62.8°); calculate average crystallite size with D = Kλ / (β cosθ) using K ≈ 0.94.

steps.title: Fourier‑transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy
steps.instruction: Place a small amount of CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC on the ATR crystal of a Bruker FTIR spectrometer; record the spectrum from 4000 to 400 cm⁻¹; note characteristic peaks such as Ti‑O stretch at 799 cm⁻¹, O‑H stretch at 3879 cm⁻¹, C = C at 2325 cm⁻¹, and C‑O stretches between 1087–1568 cm⁻¹.

steps.title: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA)
steps.instruction: Place ~X mg of CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC in the TGA pan (Q500, USA); heat from room temperature to 1000 °C at a rate of 10 °C min⁻¹ under air; record weight loss and derivative curves to assess moisture, volatile matter, and thermal stability.

steps.title: X‑ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)
steps.instruction: Introduce CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC into the XPS instrument (ESCALAB Xi+, Thermo‑Fisher); acquire a survey spectrum to confirm C, O, Ti presence; record high‑resolution spectra for C 1s, O 1s, and Ti 2p; deconvolute peaks (e.g., C 1s at 284.8, 286.1, 289.2 eV; O 1s at 530.6, 532.3 eV; Ti 2p₃/₂ at 459.4 eV, Ti 2p₁/₂ at 465.0 eV) and interpret chemical states.

steps.title: Scanning electron microscopy with EDX (SEM‑EDX)
steps.instruction: Mount a small amount of CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC on an SEM stub, coat if required; image the surface morphology using a FESEM (Verios 460 L, USA) equipped with an Oxford Instruments EDX detector; acquire elemental maps for Ti, O, C and other elements.

steps.title: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM)
steps.instruction: Disperse CSAC‑P‑TiO₂‑NC in ethanol, drop‑cast onto a carbon‑coated copper grid; observe with a high‑resolution TEM (JEOL JEM‑2100F) operating at 200 keV; capture images at various magnifications; measure particle size (≈55–60 nm) using ImageJ software.
